statement: Of all the parallelograms applied to the same straight line and deficient by parallelogrammic figures similar and similarly situated to that described on the half of the straight line, that parallelogram is greatest which is applied to the half of the straight line and is similar to the defect.
heath_proof: Let AB be a straight line and let it be bisected at C; let there be applied to the straight line AB the parallelogram AD deficient by the parallelogrammic figure DB described on the half of AB, that is, CB; I say that, of all the parallelograms applied to AB and deficient by parallelogrammic figures similar and similarly situated to DB, AD is greatest. For let there be applied to the straight line AB the parallelogram AF deficient by the parallelogrammic figure FB similar and similarly situated to DB; I say that AD is greater than AF. For, since the parallelogram DB is similar to the parallelogram FB, they are about the same diameter. [VI. 26]  Let their diameter DB be drawn, and let the figure be described. Then, since CF is equal to FE, [I. 43] and FB is common, therefore the whole CH is equal to the whole KE. But CH is equal to CG, since AC is also equal to CB. [I. 36] Therefore GC is also equal to EK. Let CF be added to each; therefore the whole AF is equal to the gnomon LMN; so that the parallelogram DB, that is, AD, is greater than the parallelogram AF.
ai_proof_text:
6.27
**Statement:** Of all the parallelograms applied to the same straight line and deficient by parallelogrammic figures similar and similarly situated to that described on the half of the straight line, that parallelogram is greatest which is applied to the half of the straight line and is similar to the defect.

**Step 1.** Let AB be the given straight line, and let it be bisected at the point E [by 1.10]. Let the parallelogram AEFD be applied to the half AE, so that the defect EF (that is, the parallelogram on EB) is similar and similarly situated to AEFD. We must show that of all parallelograms applied to AB and deficient by parallelogrammic figures similar and similarly situated to EF, the parallelogram AEFD is the greatest.

**Step 2.** Let any other parallelogram AG be applied to AB, deficient by a parallelogrammic figure GB that is similar and similarly situated to EF. We must show that AEFD is greater than AG.

**Step 3.** Since the parallelogram EF is similar and similarly situated to GB [by hypothesis], and they are parallelogrammic figures described in connection with the same line AB, while EF is the parallelogram on the half EB and GB is a different parallelogram on a portion of AB, we observe that EF and GB are similar parallelograms [D6.1].

**Step 4.** Since EF is similar and similarly situated to GB, the parallelogram EF is about the same diameter with GB [by 6.26, since GB is similar and similarly situated to EF and they share a common angle]. Let their common diameter be HB, and let the figure be described [P1].

**Step 5.** Now since EF is the parallelogram described on EB (the half of AB), and GB is the parallelogram deficient from the full line, the parallelogram EF has the diagonal HB passing through it, and GB is about the same diagonal [by 6.26].

**Step 6.** Consider the whole parallelogram EF with diagonal HB. The parallelogram GB is similar and similarly situated to EF, sharing a common angle, and is about the same diameter HB [by 6.26]. Thus GB is one of the parallelograms about the diameter of EF.

**Step 7.** In the parallelogram EF, about the diameter HB, there are parallelograms (of which GB is one), and the complements are equal to one another [by 1.43]. That is, the complement around the diameter equals the other complement.

**Step 8.** Since AE equals EB [because E is the midpoint of AB, by construction in Step 1], the parallelogram AEFD applied to AE with its corresponding configuration relates to the full parallelogram EF on EB. The parallelogram AG applied to AB is the whole figure minus the defect GB.

**Step 9.** Now the parallelogram AF (that is, AEFD) is equal to the gnomon composed of the parts of EF outside GB. Specifically, AF is the parallelogram applied to AE, and by the structure of the figure with EF about the diameter HB, the complement of GB within EF equals the complement on the other side of the diameter [by 1.43].

**Step 10.** Since EF is the parallelogram on EB with diameter HB, and GB is about the same diameter, the complements are equal [by 1.43]. The parallelogram AG equals one of these complements (namely the part of the figure between AG and GB), while AF equals the complement plus the parallelogram that lies between the two complements along the diameter.

**Step 11.** More precisely, the parallelogram AF applied to the half AE equals the gnomon formed by the whole parallelogram EF minus the inner parallelogram GB about the diameter. Meanwhile, the parallelogram AG (applied to a segment not equal to the half) equals only one complement of GB within EF [by 1.43].

**Step 12.** Since AF equals the whole parallelogram EF minus the parallelogram GB (because AF is applied to the half and EF is on the other half, and by 1.43 the complements are equal, AF equals the gnomon of EF about GB), and AG is strictly a part of this gnomon (being just one complement), it follows that AF is greater than AG.

**Step 13.** Specifically, the gnomon (which equals AF) consists of the complement AG plus an additional parallelogrammic region about the diameter. Since this additional region is a parallelogram and hence has positive area, the whole gnomon is greater than the complement alone [by CN5, the whole is greater than the part].

**Step 14.** Therefore the parallelogram AEFD applied to the half of the straight line is greater than the parallelogram AG applied to any other portion of AB, where both have defects similar and similarly situated to EF.

**Step 15.** Hence, of all the parallelograms applied to the same straight line AB and deficient by parallelogrammic figures similar and similarly situated to that described on the half of the straight line, the parallelogram applied to the half is greatest. Q.E.D.
